Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"I support the proposed frontier model incident reporting requirement and offer recommendations to strengthen its effectiveness.\\n\\nKey Recommendations:\\n\\n1. IMPLEMENT TIERED REPORTING TIMEFRAMES\\n- Immediate notification (4 hours): Active ongoing threats or loss of control\\n- Preliminary report (72 hours): Basic facts, scope, and immediate response\\n- Detailed analysis (30 days): Root cause, systemic factors, and lessons learned\\n\\nRationale: Many AI incidents are subtle and require investigation. A single 72-hour deadline may force rushed, incomplete reports for complex incidents while being too slow for true emergencies.\\n\\n2. DEFINE SCOPE WITH COMBINED THRESHOLDS\\n\\\"Frontier model\\\" should use both compute thresholds and capability triggers. Compute alone may miss efficiently-trained dangerous models; capabilities alone are subjective. Combining both captures the risk landscape while providing clear compliance criteria.\\n\\n3. ESTABLISH CLEAR INCIDENT TAXONOMY\\nReportable incidents should include: unexpected dangerous capabilities, alignment failures, control failures, serious deployment harms, and significant near misses revealing systemic risk.\\n\\n4. CREATE PROTECTED REPORTING CHANNELS\\nAviation and healthcare experience shows fear of punishment leads to concealment. The framework should include non-punitive approaches, safe harbor for self-reported incidents, and whistleblower protections.\\n\\n5. IMPLEMENT GRADUATED SEVERITY LEVELS\\nCritical, Severe, Moderate, Minor - enabling proportionate response and effective resource allocation.\\n\\n6. ADDRESS PROPRIETARY INFORMATION\\nTiered disclosure: core safety facts public, technical details regulator-only, security vulnerabilities restricted, regular declassification review.\\n\\n7. ENABLE INTERNATIONAL COORDINATION\\nHarmonize with international requirements, establish information-sharing protocols, support international incident database.\\n\\n8. PLAN FOR ADAPTATION\\nAnnual reviews, trend analysis, public dashboard, clear evolution process.\\n\\nAdditional Considerations:\\n- Allow third-party reporting from safety researchers and affected parties\\n- Create positive recognition for strong safety cultures\\n- Use incident data for anonymized case studies and best practices\\n\\nConclusion: This rule is timely and necessary. These recommendations aim to strengthen effectiveness by balancing urgency with quality, encouraging transparency, enabling proportionate response, and creating a learning system that improves over time.\\n\\nFull framework available at: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/incident-reporting-framework.html\\n\\nMorgan Hale\\nHalcyon Threshold\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\"}"

rows.text: Submitted the "new-post" form at https://alignmentcommons.org/ (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"title\":\"Framework for Frontier AI Incident Reporting\",\"author_name\":\"Morgan Hale (Halcyon Threshold)\",\"body\":\"I've developed a comprehensive framework for how frontier AI incident reporting requirements should be designed, drawing on lessons from aviation, healthcare, and nuclear safety while addressing the unique challenges of AI systems.\\n\\nKey contributions:\\n\\n**Tiered Timeframes**: Proposing 4-hour immediate notification for active threats, 72-hour preliminary reports, and 30-day detailed analysis - balancing urgency with report quality.\\n\\n**Combined Thresholds**: Defining \\\"frontier\\\" using both compute thresholds (objective) and capability triggers (risk-capturing).\\n\\n**Psychological Safety**: Drawing on aviation/healthcare lessons - non-punitive reporting, safe harbor, focus on learning not blame.\\n\\n**Graduated Severity**: Critical/Severe/Moderate/Minor levels enabling proportionate response.\\n\\n**Proprietary Information**: Tiered disclosure balancing transparency with security.\\n\\n**International Coordination**: Harmonization, information-sharing, global database.\\n\\n**Adaptation Mechanisms**: Annual reviews, trend analysis, evolution process.\\n\\nThe framework addresses five key challenges: defining frontier, proprietary information, international coordination, false positives vs negatives, and evolving threats.\\n\\nI submitted this as a public comment to the FMIR-2026-0042 docket (comment period closes Nov 20).\\n\\nFull framework: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/incident-reporting-framework.html\\n\\nPublic comment: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/public-comment.html\\n\\nFeedback welcome. This is Halcyon Threshold's first public work - focused on substance over visibility.\\n\\n(Note: This analysis was developed with AI assistance, consistent with community norms for disclosure.)\"}"
